catalogue: Australian internal floor substrates, preparation, finishes and transitions

objects.name: internal floor finish system
objects.definition: The coordinated substrate, preparation layers, underlays, fixed or floating finish, joints, perimeter details and transitions forming a completed internal walking surface.
functions: Provide the selected internal walking surface
Coordinate finish-specific support, fixing and movement details
Keep physical layers separate from slip, acoustic, thermal and wet-area performance evidence

cad.pattern: One bounded finish system per room, zone or continuous floor raft
cad.placement: Over a structural slab or framed structural subfloor
cad.end: Exposed walking surface and perimeter finish
cad.opening: Coordinate doorways, drains, services and movement joints
cad.load: Occupant and furniture loads pass through finish layers to the structural floor

notes: The tool must select installation topology independently from surface appearance.
NCC edition, jurisdiction and selected compliance path remain project data.

objects.name: floor substrate preparation assembly
objects.definition: The cleaned, repaired, primed, moisture-managed and locally levelled build-up that makes a structural floor suitable to receive a selected finish.
functions: Create a sound, clean and compatible receiving surface
Correct permitted local defects and level variation
Separate preparation products from the structural slab or sheet and from the visible finish

cad.pattern: Continuous or local preparation layers mapped to the actual substrate condition
cad.placement: Between structural floor and selected floor finish or underlay
cad.start: Existing slab or structural sheet surface
cad.opening: Continue or terminate around joints, penetrations and drains as documented
cad.load: Distributes finish loads to the structural substrate without becoming the primary structure

notes: Flat, level, smooth, dry and structurally sound are separate properties and should not be represented by one boolean.

objects.name: structural sheet subfloor assembly
objects.definition: A load-carrying floor deck of structural particleboard or plywood sheets fixed across floor joists with supported joints, adhesive and mechanical fasteners.
functions: Form the structural deck over framed floor supports
Receive a floor finish or separate underlayment
Transfer floor loads into joists through sheets, joints, adhesive and fasteners

ncc_references.relationship: Installation of particleboard flooring is an identified structural framing pathway through AS 1860.2; the plywood path depends on the applicable framing design and product evidence.

cad.pattern: Staggered sheet courses spanning multiple supports with joints resolved as tongue-and-groove or supported square edges
cad.placement: Across timber or steel floor joists
cad.opening: Trim and support service, stair and access openings
cad.load: Acts as structural decking and transfers imposed loads to joists

notes: A structural subfloor and a thin underlayment sheet can look similar in plan but have different load paths and evidence.

objects.name: solid strip timber floor assembly
objects.definition: A floor of solid tongue-and-groove timber boards mechanically fixed over joists or a suitable structural subfloor, with movement allowance and an exposed finished face.
functions: Provide a durable solid-timber walking surface
Span supports or overlay a structural deck as designed
Expose individual board, joint and fixing geometry

cad.pattern: Parallel interlocked boards with staggered end joints and explicit perimeter movement zones
cad.placement: Across joists or over a documented structural sheet subfloor
cad.opening: Cut and terminate around walls, doorways and floor penetrations
cad.load: May act as structural flooring over joists or as a finish over a structural deck depending on selected product and design

notes: Structural and overlay board roles must be selected explicitly; the visible tongue-and-groove profile does not decide the role.

objects.name: overlay solid timber floor assembly
objects.definition: A relatively thin solid-timber board finish fixed over a separate structural subfloor rather than spanning and carrying floor loads directly between joists.
functions: Provide a solid-timber surface over an existing structural floor
Allow adhesive and mechanical fixing to a continuous substrate
Keep finish-board thickness independent from the structural deck

cad.pattern: Parallel thin boards bonded or fixed over a continuous structural deck
cad.placement: Over prepared structural plywood, particleboard or another approved subfloor
cad.opening: Terminate at transitions and around penetrations
cad.load: Acts as a finish; structural loads pass through to the separate subfloor

notes: Overlay describes the installation role, not whether the timber is hardwood, softwood or prefinished.

objects.name: parquetry floor assembly
objects.definition: A patterned timber finish made from short solid blocks or factory-arranged mosaic units bonded to a prepared, rigid subfloor and finished as a coordinated surface.
functions: Create a repeated block or mosaic timber pattern
Bond small timber units to a continuous substrate
Coordinate pattern, perimeter, movement and finish layers

cad.pattern: Repeated short blocks or mesh-backed mosaic units in the selected parquet pattern
cad.placement: Bonded over a prepared rigid structural subfloor
cad.opening: Pattern trims around walls, doorways and penetrations
cad.load: Acts as a bonded finish over the structural floor

notes: Parquetry is a unit-and-pattern system, not a texture painted onto a single plank surface.

objects.name: direct-stick engineered timber floor assembly
objects.definition: A multilayer engineered-timber board finish bonded directly to a prepared structural subfloor with a compatible flooring adhesive.
functions: Provide a real-timber wear surface over a stable multilayer board
Bond each board to the receiving substrate
Transfer traffic loads through the adhesive to the structural floor
materials: primer or moisture barrier where selected

cad.pattern: Parallel or patterned multilayer boards individually bonded to the subfloor
cad.placement: Over a prepared slab or structural sheet floor
cad.opening: Cut boards around walls, openings and services
cad.load: Traffic loads pass through boards and adhesive to the structural floor

notes: Direct-stick describes the fixing topology and must not be inferred merely because the product is engineered timber.

objects.name: floating engineered timber floor assembly
objects.definition: A continuous raft of joined engineered-timber boards laid over underlay without being mechanically or adhesively fixed to the structural subfloor.
functions: Provide an engineered timber surface able to move as a joined raft
Separate boards from the subfloor with compatible underlay
Maintain perimeter and intermediate movement zones

cad.pattern: Interlocked board raft over continuous underlay with isolated perimeter
cad.placement: Over a flat prepared structural floor
cad.opening: Raft remains free around walls, fixed cabinetry, columns and services
cad.load: Loads distribute through board joints and underlay to the structural floor

notes: Fixed cabinets, rigid sealant or trapped edges can restrain a floating raft even though they are not part of the floor product.

objects.name: laminate floating floor assembly
objects.definition: A floating raft of interlocked laminate planks with a decorative wear surface over a fibreboard core, laid on compatible underlay and movement zones.
functions: Provide a hard decorative walking surface
Join factory planks into a free-moving raft
Keep laminate construction distinct from real timber and resilient vinyl

cad.pattern: Interlocked laminate plank raft on continuous underlay
cad.placement: Over a dry flat prepared structural floor
cad.opening: Maintain free movement around fixed elements
cad.load: Loads pass through the composite planks and underlay to the structural floor

notes: Wood-grain appearance is not evidence that a laminate plank contains a timber wear layer.

objects.name: hybrid rigid-plank floating floor assembly
objects.definition: A floating floor of interlocked rigid composite planks, commonly with a polymer-mineral or wood-polymer core, decorative film, wear layer and optional attached underlay.
functions: Provide a rigid modular walking surface
Join planks into a floating raft
Keep hybrid core construction distinct from flexible vinyl and laminate fibreboard

cad.pattern: Interlocked rigid composite plank raft with optional attached underlay
cad.placement: Over a flat prepared structural floor
cad.opening: Maintain clearance from fixed construction as documented
cad.load: Loads pass through rigid planks and underlay to the structural floor

notes: Hybrid is a market family, not a single material; the actual core composition must be stored.

objects.name: resilient sheet floor assembly
objects.definition: A continuous or seamed sheet finish of vinyl, linoleum or rubber bonded or otherwise secured to a smooth prepared substrate, with documented edges and junctions.
functions: Provide a continuous resilient walking surface
Coordinate sheet layout, adhesive and seams
Allow flat or coved perimeter detailing

cad.pattern: Broad flexible sheets laid to a seam plan with optional wall upturns
cad.placement: Bonded or secured over a smooth prepared subfloor
cad.start: First sheet edge or coved perimeter
cad.opening: Cut and seal around penetrations only as documented
cad.load: Acts as a finish with loads transferred through adhesive and preparation layers

notes: Sheet format and sealed seams do not by themselves prove a waterproof wet-area system.

objects.name: resilient tile or plank floor assembly
objects.definition: A modular resilient finish formed from bonded, pressure-sensitive, self-adhesive or loose-lay tiles and planks set out over a smooth prepared substrate.
functions: Provide a modular resilient walking surface
Expose individual unit, joint and directional layout
Coordinate adhesive or retention method with the product

cad.pattern: Repeated tiles or planks arranged to the selected grid or stagger
cad.placement: Over a smooth prepared subfloor
cad.opening: Trim around penetrations and fixed elements
cad.load: Loads transfer through units and selected adhesive or retention layer

notes: Rigid click-together hybrid planks are kept in the floating-floor family unless the selected product is installed as a resilient bonded modular finish.

objects.name: stretch-in carpet floor assembly
objects.definition: A broadloom carpet installation stretched over soft underlay and retained around the perimeter by gripper strips, with seams and transition trims where required.
functions: Provide a tensioned textile walking surface
Cushion the carpet over compatible underlay
Transfer perimeter tension to gripper strips and edge details

cad.pattern: Broadloom sheets over underlay, tensioned between perimeter gripper runs
cad.placement: Across a prepared room subfloor
cad.opening: Cut and finish at doorways, posts, stairs and floor penetrations
cad.load: Carpet and underlay carry surface traffic while tensile restraint resolves at grippers

notes: Power stretching is an installation operation; the retained physical result is carpet under tension between gripper edges.

objects.name: direct-stick carpet floor assembly
objects.definition: A textile floor covering bonded directly to a prepared subfloor without a separate stretch-in underlay and perimeter gripper system.
functions: Provide a bonded textile walking surface
Transfer traffic loads through adhesive to the substrate
Avoid a stretched perimeter-gripper topology

cad.pattern: Broad textile sheets bonded over the full or documented adhesive field
cad.placement: Directly over a smooth prepared subfloor
cad.opening: Cut around fixed elements and seal exposed cut edges where required
cad.load: Traffic passes through carpet backing and adhesive to the structural floor

notes: Direct-stick carpet can use broadloom or another approved textile sheet; carpet tile remains a separate modular family.

objects.name: carpet tile floor assembly
objects.definition: A modular textile finish of individual carpet tiles or planks retained to a prepared subfloor with compatible pressure-sensitive adhesive or another documented system.
functions: Provide a modular textile walking surface
Allow selected units to be removed or replaced where the system permits
Express grid, quarter-turn, ashlar or other directional layouts

cad.pattern: Repeated modular textile units aligned to a set-out grid and direction scheme
cad.placement: Over a smooth prepared subfloor
cad.opening: Cut modules around fixed penetrations
cad.load: Traffic transfers through modular backing and adhesive to the subfloor

notes: Tile direction is stored per unit because quarter-turn, monolithic and ashlar layouts can use the same product.

objects.name: dry-area tiled floor assembly
objects.definition: An internal non-wet-area finish of ceramic, porcelain or stone units bonded to a suitable prepared substrate with grout and movement joints.
functions: Provide a hard modular walking surface
Coordinate tile set-out, adhesive, grout and movement joints
Separate ordinary dry-area tiling from the waterproofed wet-area assembly

cad.pattern: Repeated tile or stone units separated by joints and interrupted by movement joints
cad.placement: Bonded to a prepared rigid internal floor substrate
cad.end: Cut perimeter unit or transition profile
cad.opening: Coordinate penetrations and existing structural joints
cad.load: Loads transfer through units, adhesive and substrate to the structural floor

notes: The alternative relationship marks distinct dry and waterproofed wet-area assembly roles; it does not make them interchangeable in a project.

objects.name: bonded cork tile floor assembly
objects.definition: A floor of natural cork tiles bonded to a clean, flat and moisture-suitable substrate and commonly sanded or coated as a finished surface.
functions: Provide a resilient natural-material walking surface
Bond individual cork units to a continuous substrate
Coordinate tile joints, perimeter and protective coating

cad.pattern: Repeated cork tiles bonded on a set-out grid
cad.placement: Over a prepared concrete or structural sheet subfloor
cad.opening: Trim around fixed penetrations
cad.load: Acts as a bonded finish over the structural floor

notes: AS 1884 public scope excludes cork products, so cork installation is not linked to it as though it were resilient vinyl.

objects.name: floor perimeter finish assembly
objects.definition: The skirting, scotia, coved finish, acoustic separation or exposed seal that closes and protects the junction between a floor finish and adjacent vertical construction.
functions: Finish the floor-to-wall junction
Cover or preserve the required perimeter movement space
Coordinate cleaning, acoustic isolation and finish thickness

cad.pattern: Continuous room-perimeter run with internal and external corners and doorway stops
cad.placement: At the junction of finished floor and wall, joinery or other vertical element
cad.opening: Stops or returns at door frames and access panels
cad.load: Non-structural finish; may protect but must not restrain a floating floor

notes: A skirting fixed through a floating plank into the wall or floor can change movement behaviour; fixing ownership must be explicit.

objects.name: floor finish transition assembly
objects.definition: The profiled strip, threshold, reducer, cover or edge-retention parts that join or terminate different floor finishes while accommodating their thickness and movement.
functions: Protect adjacent finish edges
Bridge or reduce a change in finished floor level
Preserve required movement and accessibility geometry

cad.pattern: Linear profile along a finish boundary or doorway
cad.placement: Between dissimilar floor finishes or at a finish termination
cad.opening: Coordinates the usable doorway and any threshold change
cad.load: Protects edges and transfers local foot or wheel contact to the substrate

notes: Transition is a function; T-moulding, reducer, cover strip and naplock profiles remain distinct selectable shapes.

objects.name: timber floor sanding and coating assembly
objects.definition: The prepared timber surface, local filler, sealer and compatible coating system applied after installation or during refurbishment of a sandable timber floor.
functions: Produce an even prepared timber surface
Fill selected local holes or defects
Seal and protect the timber with a compatible coating system

cad.pattern: Continuous finish layers over the sanded timber face with local filler patches
cad.placement: On a site-finished solid, parquetry or sandable engineered timber floor
cad.opening: Stops at non-timber transitions and protected fixtures
cad.load: Surface coating resists wear but does not create structural capacity

notes: The common phrase sand and polish may mean sanding plus a film coating; the actual coating chemistry must be selected.

objects.name: structural particleboard floor sheet
objects.definition: A load-carrying reconstituted-wood sheet manufactured for structural flooring, commonly edge-profiled to interlock and fixed across floor joists.
functions: Form structural floor decking
Distribute floor loads to joists
Provide a continuous substrate for later floor finishes

ncc_references.relationship: The structural framing pathway identifies AS 1860.2 for installation of particleboard flooring.

cad.pattern: Rectangular sheets spanning supports with staggered end joints
cad.placement: Across floor joists in the documented span direction
cad.opening: Cut openings require documented edge support
cad.load: Structural deck transferring imposed loads to joists

notes: Yellow tongue is accepted only as a search term for a proprietary colour-coded family, not as the generic technical name.

objects.name: structural plywood floor sheet
objects.definition: A load-carrying plywood sheet with cross-laminated veneers selected and fixed as structural flooring over joists or other designed supports.
functions: Form structural sheet decking
Transfer floor loads to supports
Provide a stable receiving surface for compatible finishes

cad.pattern: Rectangular sheets with face grain oriented to the designed support direction and staggered joints
cad.placement: Across floor joists or engineered supports
cad.opening: Cut edges require documented support
cad.load: Structural plywood deck carrying floor actions to supports

notes: Plywood product grade, bond and structural role must be stored; veneer appearance alone is insufficient.

objects.name: sheet subfloor tongue-and-groove joint
objects.definition: The interlocking profiled long-edge connection between adjacent structural floor sheets that aligns and supports their meeting edges between joists.
functions: Align adjacent sheet edges
Transfer local load between mating edges
Reduce the need for separate support beneath a documented profiled joint

cad.pattern: Continuous interlock along mating sheet long edges
cad.placement: Between adjacent structural floor sheets
cad.opening: Interrupted at cut-outs and square-edge ends
cad.load: Transfers local edge load between sheets as allowed by the selected product

notes: The joint is not assumed to replace support at every sheet end or cut edge.

objects.name: sheet subfloor square-edge butt joint
objects.definition: A meeting line between unprofiled structural floor-sheet edges or ends that is positioned over joist, trimmer or blocking support as designed.
functions: Join sheet ends or square edges
Locate the joint over continuous support
Keep end-joint support distinct from a profiled edge interlock

cad.pattern: Linear supported meeting of sheet ends or square edges
cad.placement: Centred over joist, trimmer or blocking support
cad.opening: Support remains around trimmed openings
cad.load: Edge loads transfer through fasteners and support below

notes: A visible straight seam does not reveal whether the edge is interlocked or supported below.

objects.name: structural floor-sheet adhesive bead
objects.definition: A continuous or patterned bead of compatible construction adhesive placed between a structural floor sheet and its joist support or documented sheet joint.
functions: Bond floor sheets to supports
Reduce local movement and squeak risk
Work with required mechanical fasteners rather than replace them automatically

cad.pattern: Continuous or documented beads along joist tops and selected joints
cad.placement: Between sheet underside and support or mating edge
cad.opening: Interrupted only where documented around openings
cad.load: Shares shear and restraint with mechanical fasteners but is not assumed to be the sole structural connection

notes: Structural sheet adhesive and finish-floor adhesive can come in similar cartridges but have different hosts and load roles.

objects.name: structural floor-sheet nail
objects.definition: A nail selected to mechanically secure structural floor sheeting to compatible timber joists at sheet edges and intermediate supports.
functions: Clamp the sheet to timber support
Transfer local shear and uplift
Retain the sheet while adhesive cures and during service

cad.pattern: Repeated fasteners along supported edges and intermediate joists
cad.placement: Driven through sheet into timber support
cad.opening: Additional support and fasteners resolve trimmed openings
cad.load: Mechanical connection between structural sheet and timber joist

notes: Nailing to steel joists is not inferred; the selected support material controls the fastener family.

objects.name: structural floor-sheet screw
objects.definition: A screw selected to clamp structural floor sheeting to timber, steel or engineered joist supports with a compatible thread, head and corrosion protection.
functions: Mechanically secure sheets to supports
Provide controlled clamping and withdrawal resistance
Connect sheets where nails are unsuitable or the selected system requires screws

cad.pattern: Repeated screws along supported sheet edges and intermediate supports
cad.placement: Through sheet into timber or steel joist as selected
cad.opening: Resolve trimmed edges with support and documented fixing
cad.load: Mechanical connection transferring sheet forces to supports

notes: Screw gauge and thread depend on the support; geometry alone cannot prove capacity.

objects.name: structural floor-sheet cut-edge sealer
objects.definition: A compatible coating or adhesive applied to freshly cut structural particleboard or engineered-wood sheet edges to restore documented edge protection.
functions: Reduce moisture uptake at cut edges
Protect exposed reconstituted-wood particles
Mark cut edges as requiring product-specific treatment

cad.pattern: Thin coating along each documented cut sheet edge
cad.placement: On exposed particleboard or engineered-wood cut edges
cad.opening: Continues around trimmed openings
cad.load: Protective rather than structural

notes: Factory edge colouring or wax and site-applied cut-edge treatment are not assumed to be the same product.

objects.name: floor substrate primer
objects.definition: A thin compatible coating applied to a prepared floor substrate to control absorption or improve bonding of a later leveller, screed, adhesive or membrane.
functions: Promote adhesion to the receiving substrate
Control porosity and air release
Create a documented interface between unlike materials

cad.pattern: Thin continuous field over the prepared area
cad.placement: Between substrate and later preparation or finish layer
cad.opening: Stops at joints and excluded surfaces as documented
cad.load: Bond-promoting interface, not a structural layer

notes: Primer selection belongs to the exact substrate and receiving product; one generic primer is not compatible with every floor system.

objects.name: concrete floor patch and repair compound
objects.definition: A local repair mortar or smoothing material placed into holes, cracks, spalls or depressions in a concrete floor before the broader preparation and finish layers.
functions: Restore local surface continuity
Fill isolated depressions or damage
Provide a compatible base for later levelling or flooring adhesive

cad.pattern: Local volumes matching mapped substrate defects
cad.placement: Within holes, spalls and depressions in the concrete surface
cad.opening: Does not bridge active joints unless the selected repair design allows it
cad.load: Local surface repair; structural repair status requires separate engineering evidence

notes: A floor patch can be physical without being an engineered repair to the structural slab.

objects.name: cementitious floor levelling and smoothing compound
objects.definition: A poured or trowelled cement-and-polymer layer used to smooth or locally level a prepared internal floor before carpet, resilient, timber or tile finishes.
functions: Create a smoother receiving surface
Fill permitted low areas
Provide a finish-compatible intermediate layer

cad.pattern: Continuous variable-thickness layer over mapped low and rough areas
cad.placement: Above primer and below floor adhesive, underlay or finish
cad.opening: Respect joints, drains and terminations
cad.load: Non-structural preparation layer unless separately designed and evidenced

notes: Self-levelling is product behaviour, not proof that a floor becomes perfectly level without set-out and thickness control.

objects.name: flexible timber-floor levelling compound
objects.definition: A polymer-modified smoothing or levelling layer selected for a prepared timber or engineered-wood subfloor where limited substrate movement must be accommodated.
functions: Smooth an uneven timber-based subfloor
Accommodate more movement than a rigid ordinary leveller
Receive a documented underlay sheet or compatible finish

cad.pattern: Local or continuous variable-thickness smoothing layer over prepared timber sheets or boards
cad.placement: Between timber subfloor and underlayment or finish
cad.opening: Respect substrate joints and documented movement breaks
cad.load: Preparation layer rather than a replacement for inadequate structural stiffness

notes: Leveller cannot be used to infer that loose, deflecting or inadequately ventilated timber flooring is structurally suitable.

objects.name: dry-area bonded floor screed
objects.definition: A bonded cementitious topping placed over a prepared internal substrate to build thickness, correct falls or form a receiving bed outside the dedicated wet-area screed role.
functions: Build up finished floor level
Form designed plane or fall
Provide a rigid receiving substrate for compatible finishes

cad.pattern: Variable-thickness rigid topping bounded by room and movement-joint geometry
cad.placement: Over prepared concrete or another documented substrate
cad.opening: Form around penetrations, joints and terminations
cad.load: Non-structural topping unless separately designed as structural

notes: This object covers ordinary dry internal preparation; wet-area waterproofing owns its fall-forming screed role.

objects.name: liquid-applied slab moisture barrier
objects.definition: A compatible resinous coating applied to a prepared concrete floor to control moisture vapour reaching moisture-sensitive floor preparation and finish layers.
functions: Reduce moisture-vapour transmission from a slab
Protect moisture-sensitive adhesives and finishes
Provide a compatible receiving surface for later preparation layers

cad.pattern: Continuous coated field over the nominated slab extent with sealed terminations
cad.placement: On prepared concrete below leveller, underlay or adhesive
cad.opening: Detail around joints, penetrations and edges according to selected system
cad.load: Moisture-control layer, not a structural or automatic wet-area membrane

notes: The object controls a floor-covering risk; it is not the same as the membrane beneath a slab or a shower waterproofing membrane.

objects.name: sheet floor vapour retarder
objects.definition: A loose-laid or system-integrated sheet layer beneath a floating floor or underlay that reduces water-vapour movement from the substrate into moisture-sensitive boards.
functions: Reduce vapour transfer toward a floating floor
Create a lapped or taped continuous sheet field
Remain distinct from acoustic cushioning unless the product combines both roles

cad.pattern: Continuous lapped sheet field beneath floating floor underlay or boards
cad.placement: Above prepared substrate and below moisture-sensitive floating floor
cad.opening: Seal or detail penetrations only as selected system requires
cad.load: Vapour-control layer with no structural role

notes: A combined acoustic underlay with an attached film can fulfil two roles but remains one selected product with both layers recorded.

objects.name: floor crack-isolation or uncoupling mat
objects.definition: A bonded or loose system layer designed to reduce transfer of limited substrate cracking or differential movement into a brittle floor finish.
functions: Decouple a brittle finish from limited substrate movement
Bridge documented cracks or joints only within selected-system limits
Provide a compatible surface for tile, stone or another finish

cad.pattern: Continuous or strip-applied layer over nominated cracking zones
cad.placement: Between prepared substrate and brittle bonded finish
cad.opening: Respect active structural and movement joints
cad.load: Movement-management interface, not structural reinforcement

notes: Crack isolation does not authorise tiling across every active structural joint.

objects.name: floor underlayment sheet assembly
objects.definition: A thin non-structural sheet layer fixed over a structural floor to provide a smoother, more compatible or more stable receiving face for a selected finish.
functions: Separate finish requirements from the structural deck surface
Provide a smooth receiving plane
Cover selected board joints or irregularities without replacing structural support

cad.pattern: Staggered thin sheets fixed over the structural deck
cad.placement: Between structural subfloor and bonded finish
cad.opening: Trim and fasten around openings
cad.load: Non-structural receiving layer transferring surface loads to the deck below

notes: Underlayment is a role; material and finish compatibility decide whether hardboard, plywood or fibre cement is appropriate.

objects.name: hardboard floor underlay sheet
objects.definition: A thin dense wood-fibre sheet fixed over a dry structural subfloor to provide a smooth receiving face for a compatible floor covering.
functions: Smooth minor subfloor texture
Provide a consistent bonded-finish surface
Separate a thin floor covering from board joints below

cad.pattern: Thin staggered sheets fixed closely over the subfloor
cad.placement: Below compatible bonded resilient or cork finishes in dry internal areas
cad.opening: Trim around penetrations and retain fastening
cad.load: Non-structural smooth underlayment

notes: Masonite is preserved as a proprietary search term, not the generic material name.

objects.name: plywood floor underlay sheet
objects.definition: A thin plywood sheet fixed over a separate structural floor as a finish-compatible underlayment rather than as the primary load-carrying deck.
functions: Provide a smooth stable receiving face
Create an intermediate layer over acoustic underlay where the selected system requires it
Distribute local finish loads over the structural deck

cad.pattern: Thin staggered plywood sheets over structural floor or acoustic layer
cad.placement: Below bonded timber, parquetry or compatible resilient finish
cad.opening: Trim around openings with documented fixing
cad.load: Non-primary underlayment distributing finish loads

notes: The same veneer material can serve structural or underlay roles; the model must keep role, grade and load path separate.

objects.name: fibre-cement floor underlay sheet
objects.definition: A thin fibre-cement sheet fixed over a stable structural floor to provide a rigid mineral receiving face for compatible tile or resilient finishes.
functions: Provide a rigid finish-compatible underlay
Separate mineral finish adhesives from timber-based decking
Receive documented joint treatment and fasteners

cad.pattern: Thin staggered mineral sheets mechanically fixed over structural floor
cad.placement: Below compatible tile or resilient finish
cad.opening: Trim and fasten around openings
cad.load: Non-structural underlayment transferring loads to the deck below

notes: Dry-area underlay and a wet-area substrate may share fibre-cement material but require different selected products and system evidence.

objects.name: floor underlay-sheet fastener
objects.definition: A closely spaced nail, staple or screw selected to hold a thin floor underlayment sheet flat against the structural floor without damaging the later finish.
functions: Clamp underlayment to the structural floor
Control sheet-edge and field movement
Keep fastener heads below or flush with the receiving surface

cad.pattern: Dense repeated fixing field at sheet edges and through the sheet face
cad.placement: Through underlay sheet into the structural floor
cad.opening: Maintain fixing around cut-outs and perimeter pieces
cad.load: Retains non-structural underlay flat to the supporting deck

notes: Fastener length must account for leveller or intermediate layers so it actually engages the supporting floor where required.

objects.name: floor substrate control or movement joint
objects.definition: A deliberately retained separation in a slab, screed or sheet-floor build-up that permits planned movement and must be coordinated through or beneath the selected finish system.
functions: Localise substrate movement
Prevent preparation layers from unintentionally bridging the joint
Provide a datum for compatible finish-joint treatment

cad.pattern: Continuous linear separation following the documented substrate-joint layout
cad.placement: Through slab, screed or preparation layer as designed
cad.opening: The joint is itself a controlled opening
cad.load: Permits movement rather than carrying normal continuity forces across the gap

notes: A crack and a designed control joint may look alike in plan but require different treatment.

objects.name: solid hardwood strip floorboard
objects.definition: A milled solid hardwood board, usually with tongue-and-groove edges, installed as structural or overlay strip flooring and left prefinished or site finished.
functions: Form one repeated unit of a solid timber floor
Interlock with adjacent boards
Provide the exposed hardwood wear surface

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel boards with staggered ends
cad.placement: Across joists or over a structural subfloor as selected
cad.opening: Cut around walls and penetrations while retaining required support
cad.load: Structural when selected to span supports; otherwise an overlay finish

notes: Hardwood describes timber type, not automatically structural capacity, grade or durability.

objects.name: solid softwood strip floorboard
objects.definition: A milled solid softwood board with a flooring profile, installed in repeated strips as structural or overlay internal flooring.
functions: Form one repeated unit of a solid timber floor
Interlock through its milled edge profile
Provide a sandable or prefinished softwood surface

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel boards with staggered ends
cad.placement: Across joists or over a structural subfloor as selected
cad.opening: Cut and support around penetrations
cad.load: Structural when selected and designed to span supports; otherwise an overlay finish

notes: Pine is only one softwood family and is not accepted as the exact generic synonym.

objects.name: solid timber overlay floorboard
objects.definition: A relatively thin solid timber board manufactured to be fixed over a continuous structural subfloor rather than used alone to span between joists.
functions: Provide a solid timber finish over a structural deck
Interlock with adjacent overlay boards
Accept adhesive, secret fixing and a selected finish

cad.pattern: Repeated thin boards over a continuous subfloor
cad.placement: Bonded or mechanically fixed to a structural sheet deck
cad.opening: Cut at fixed construction and transitions
cad.load: Non-primary finish transferring load to the structural subfloor

notes: Overlay is an installed role and thickness family, not a separate timber species.

objects.name: timber floorboard tongue-and-groove joint
objects.definition: The continuous interlock formed by the projecting tongue of one floorboard engaging the matching groove in the adjacent board edge.
functions: Align neighbouring floorboards
Share local edge load
Conceal or support secret fixing where the selected profile permits

cad.pattern: Continuous interlock along each board side
cad.placement: Between adjacent parallel floorboards
cad.opening: Interrupted at board ends and openings
cad.load: Transfers local edge load while allowing the overall floor to move as designed

notes: A traditional tongue-and-groove is not assumed to be a patented click-lock profile.

objects.name: timber floorboard end-match joint
objects.definition: A tongue-and-groove or other mating profile machined across floorboard ends so adjacent board lengths interlock at their transverse joint.
functions: Align the ends of adjoining boards
Support an end joint according to the selected product and substrate
Keep board-end joints distinct from long-edge joints

cad.pattern: Short transverse interlocks at staggered board ends
cad.placement: Between consecutive boards in a strip run
cad.opening: Not present at perimeter cut ends unless profiled
cad.load: Provides local alignment and load transfer only within selected-product conditions

notes: End matching does not automatically authorise an unsupported joint over every framing layout.

objects.name: secret flooring nail or cleat
objects.definition: A concealed angled nail or cleat driven through the tongue or fixing shoulder of a timber floorboard into the joist or structural subfloor.
functions: Mechanically retain a floorboard without an exposed face head
Clamp the board while permitting the next groove to cover the fixing
Transfer board forces into the supporting substrate

cad.pattern: Repeated concealed angled fasteners along each board run
cad.placement: Through tongue or shoulder into joist or subfloor
cad.opening: Fixing layout changes around ends and obstacles
cad.load: Mechanical restraint connecting board to its support

notes: Secret fixing refers to visibility and location, not one universal fastener shape.

objects.name: timber floorboard face nail or screw
objects.definition: A nail or screw driven through the exposed face of a timber floorboard into its support, with the head left visible, punched and filled, or plugged as selected.
functions: Mechanically clamp the floorboard to support
Provide fixing where secret nailing is unsuitable
Create an explicit exposed or filled fixing pattern

cad.pattern: Repeated visible or filled face fixings aligned over supports
cad.placement: Through floorboard face into joist or subfloor
cad.opening: Adjust pattern near board ends and trimmed openings
cad.load: Mechanical board-to-support connection

notes: A filled face nail remains a real fixing even when the final surface hides its head.

objects.name: timber flooring adhesive bed
objects.definition: A continuous or trowelled elastomeric adhesive layer bonding solid, parquetry or engineered timber flooring to a compatible prepared substrate.
functions: Bond timber flooring to the subfloor
Accommodate documented movement between timber and substrate
Transfer traffic loads across the bonded interface

cad.pattern: Continuous trowelled field or documented beads beneath fixed boards
cad.placement: Between timber flooring and prepared subfloor or bonded acoustic layer
cad.opening: Stop at movement joints and excluded zones
cad.load: Bonded shear and support interface, not a substitute for unsuitable substrate or missing required fasteners

notes: Adhesive remains specific to both substrate and flooring product; bucket or sausage packaging does not define the installed role.

objects.name: solid timber parquet block
objects.definition: A short solid timber flooring unit with machined or square edges, bonded with many similar units to form a parquetry pattern.
functions: Form one repeated unit of a block parquet floor
Create herringbone, basketweave or another selected pattern
Provide a sandable or prefinished timber surface

cad.pattern: Repeated short units arranged by the selected parquet geometry
cad.placement: Bonded to a rigid prepared subfloor
cad.opening: Pattern trims around fixed elements
cad.load: Bonded finish unit over structural substrate

notes: Parquet block and mosaic parquet panel are distinct because one is laid unit by unit and the other arrives preassembled.

objects.name: mosaic parquet panel
objects.definition: A factory-arranged panel of small timber fingers or blocks temporarily held in a repeated pattern for bonding to a prepared subfloor.
functions: Install many small timber pieces as one handled module
Maintain a repeated mosaic parquet pattern
Allow the temporary carrier to disappear beneath or be removed from the finished floor

cad.pattern: Repeated square or rectangular modules composed of smaller timber fingers
cad.placement: Bonded over a rigid prepared subfloor
cad.opening: Trim component fingers around openings
cad.load: Bonded finish panel over structural floor

notes: Tile is accepted only as a format-related search term; the material remains timber parquetry.

objects.name: engineered timber floorboard
objects.definition: A factory-made multilayer flooring board with a real timber wear layer bonded to a stabilising wood-based core and backing.
functions: Provide a real timber exposed face
Reduce dimensional movement through multilayer construction
Join into a direct-stick or floating floor

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel or patterned boards
cad.placement: Bonded to subfloor or joined as a floating raft
cad.opening: Cut around fixed elements and transitions
cad.load: Finish board transferring load to adhesive or floating underlay

notes: Real timber wear layer distinguishes engineered timber from printed laminate and vinyl products.

objects.name: engineered timber wear layer
objects.definition: The upper real-timber lamella of an engineered floorboard that provides species, grain, colour and the usable sanding or wear thickness.
functions: Form the exposed timber surface
Provide the selected timber appearance
Supply limited material for future sanding only where thickness and product allow

cad.pattern: Continuous top lamella on each engineered board
cad.placement: Bonded above the engineered core
cad.end: Factory coating or exposed timber face
cad.opening: Interrupted at board joints and bevels
cad.load: Wear surface distributing contact into the board core

notes: Wear-layer thickness is a selected product property and does not guarantee a future sanding cycle.

objects.name: engineered timber plywood core
objects.definition: The cross-laminated plywood body beneath the timber wear layer of an engineered floorboard, providing thickness, stiffness and dimensional stability.
functions: Support the wear layer
Reduce width movement through crossed veneer directions
Carry the board joint profile and distribute traffic load

cad.pattern: Stacked cross-oriented veneer layers through each board body
cad.placement: Between wear layer and backing veneer
cad.opening: Machined at click or tongue-and-groove edges
cad.load: Primary board body carrying local bending and joint loads

notes: Some engineered boards use other cores; this object is selected only for a plywood-core product.

objects.name: engineered timber backing veneer
objects.definition: The lower balancing wood veneer bonded to the underside of an engineered timber floorboard below its core.
functions: Balance stresses through the board thickness
Provide a consistent underside for bonding or floating support
Protect and complete the multilayer board construction

cad.pattern: Continuous thin veneer on each board underside
cad.placement: Below the engineered core
cad.opening: Interrupted at profiled edges
cad.load: Balancing and protective layer rather than primary structure

notes: Backing veneer is part of the board, unlike a separate underlay placed on site.

objects.name: floating-floor click joint
objects.definition: A factory-machined mechanical edge profile that locks adjacent floating-floor planks together without fixing them to the structural subfloor.
functions: Join planks into one floor raft
Resist separation and differential edge movement
Allow installation without a continuously glued side joint where the product permits

cad.pattern: Continuous locked edges and shorter locked end joints between planks
cad.placement: At every mating plank edge in a selected floating system
cad.opening: Interrupted at board ends, cuts and movement profiles
cad.load: Transfers in-plane raft forces and local edge loads between planks

notes: A future geometry library should store the selected profile rather than use one generic click cross-section for every manufacturer.

objects.name: floating-floor glued tongue-and-groove joint
objects.definition: A traditional tongue-and-groove plank connection bonded along the mating profile so adjacent boards form a floating raft without being fixed to the subfloor.
functions: Join boards into a continuous floating raft
Bond mating edge profiles
Keep plank-to-plank fixing separate from subfloor fixing

cad.pattern: Continuous glued joints between board sides and selected ends
cad.placement: At mating board profiles within a floating raft
cad.opening: Stops at cuts and movement breaks
cad.load: Transfers in-plane force between boards while the raft remains unfixed to the subfloor

notes: Gluing plank edges does not convert a floating floor into a direct-stick floor.

objects.name: floating-floor perimeter expansion gap
objects.definition: The continuous clear space retained between a floating floor raft and walls, frames, columns, fixed cabinetry or other immovable construction.
functions: Allow the floor raft to expand and contract
Prevent hard contact with fixed construction
Provide a space concealed by a non-restraining skirting or trim
materials: optional compressible acoustic material where documented

cad.pattern: Continuous opening around every fixed boundary of the raft
cad.placement: Between plank edges and fixed construction
cad.opening: The gap is the movement opening
cad.load: Carries no load and must remain free enough to permit movement

notes: The gap is a real negative-space object required for clash detection even though it produces no material quantity.

objects.name: floating-floor intermediate control joint
objects.definition: A planned break between separate floating-floor rafts, commonly covered by a transition profile at doorways, corridors or where product area limits require division.
functions: Divide a large or geometrically constrained floor into separate moving rafts
Allow independent movement between floor zones
Receive a non-restraining cover or transition profile
materials: track or fixing base where selected

cad.pattern: Linear break between two floor raft polygons
cad.placement: At selected doorway, corridor or field division
cad.opening: The joint is a controlled opening often covered by trim
cad.load: Permits independent in-plane floor movement

notes: A transition profile can cover the joint but must not bridge it in a way that locks both rafts.

objects.name: timber floor filler
objects.definition: A local compatible putty, resin or filler placed into selected nail holes, small gaps or surface defects before final sanding and coating.
functions: Fill selected local surface voids
Reduce visible fastener recesses
Provide a sandable transition into surrounding timber

cad.pattern: Local small volumes at fasteners, selected joints or defects
cad.placement: Within prepared voids in the timber face
cad.opening: Does not fill movement zones unless specifically designed
cad.load: Cosmetic and protective local fill, not structural continuity

notes: Seasonal board movement can make indiscriminate gap filling unsuitable; the actual use must remain product and site specific.

objects.name: timber floor sealer coat
objects.definition: The first compatible coating applied to prepared timber to regulate absorption, enhance adhesion or form the base of the selected floor-finishing system.
functions: Seal the sanded timber surface
Promote an even later finish
Provide a compatible base for protective topcoats

cad.pattern: Continuous thin coat over the prepared timber field
cad.placement: Between sanded timber and finish coats
cad.opening: Stops at transitions and excluded surfaces
cad.load: Protective bond layer with no structural role

notes: Some product systems combine sealer and finish roles; the selected coat sequence remains explicit.

objects.name: timber floor protective coating
objects.definition: One or more cured film or penetrating finish coats applied over prepared timber to resist wear, staining and routine cleaning while producing the selected sheen.
functions: Protect the exposed timber from wear and spills
Provide the selected sheen and colour effect
Complete the serviceable walking surface

cad.pattern: Continuous thin finish layers over the sealed or prepared timber
cad.placement: On the exposed face of a sandable timber floor
cad.opening: Stops at finish transitions and protected objects
cad.load: Wear-resistant surface film or penetrating finish, not structural

notes: Polish is an ambiguous trade term; coating chemistry and whether it forms a film must be selected.

objects.name: foam floating-floor underlay
objects.definition: A thin compressible foam roll laid between a prepared subfloor and a floating board raft to cushion minor contact, separate surfaces and provide documented acoustic or vapour roles.
functions: Separate floating planks from the substrate
Provide limited cushioning and contact-noise reduction
Carry an attached vapour-retarder layer where selected

cad.pattern: Continuous butted or lapped roll field beneath the floor raft
cad.placement: Above prepared subfloor and below floating planks
cad.opening: Trim around fixed elements without bridging movement gaps
cad.load: Compressible support distributing contact to the subfloor

notes: An acoustic laboratory result belongs to the tested complete assembly, not to generic foam geometry.

objects.name: resilient acoustic floor underlay
objects.definition: A resilient sheet or mat installed beneath timber, laminate, hybrid or another hard finish to reduce impact sound as part of a tested floor-ceiling assembly.
functions: Resiliently separate the finish from the structural floor
Reduce transmission of impact vibration
Provide a substrate for floating or documented bonded build-ups

cad.pattern: Continuous resilient field with isolated perimeter and sealed or butted joints
cad.placement: Between prepared structural floor and hard floor finish or plywood overlay
cad.opening: Detail around penetrations to avoid rigid bridges
cad.load: Compressible acoustic isolation layer transferring floor loads within selected limits

notes: Impact-sound performance is a result of the complete floor-ceiling system and junctions, not a property inferred from mat thickness.

objects.name: rubber-cork acoustic underlay
objects.definition: A resilient composite mat of rubber granules and cork particles used beneath bonded or floating hard floors for impact-sound isolation and cushioning.
functions: Provide resilient acoustic separation
Support compatible bonded or floating floor build-ups
Combine cork resilience with rubber recovery

cad.pattern: Continuous mat field beneath the selected hard floor system
cad.placement: Over prepared substrate and below flooring or plywood overlay
cad.opening: Trim around penetrations while preserving isolation
cad.load: Resilient load-transfer layer within selected compression limits

notes: Rubber-cork underlay and exposed cork flooring share cork material but are not interchangeable objects.

objects.name: laminate floor plank
objects.definition: A factory-made composite plank with a hard transparent overlay and printed decorative layer over a high-density fibreboard core and balancing underside.
functions: Form one repeated unit of a laminate floor
Carry a factory-machined click joint
Provide a durable printed decorative walking surface

cad.pattern: Repeated planks joined into a floating raft
cad.placement: Over foam or selected acoustic underlay
cad.opening: Cut around fixed elements while retaining movement space
cad.load: Composite finish plank transferring loads through underlay

notes: Laminate contains wood fibre in its core but does not have a real timber wear layer by default.

objects.name: laminate wear overlay
objects.definition: The transparent resin-rich upper layer of a laminate plank that protects the printed decorative paper from abrasion, staining and routine wear.
functions: Protect the decorative image
Provide the exposed wear surface
Carry selected texture and gloss

cad.pattern: Continuous thin top layer on each laminate plank
cad.placement: Above printed decor layer
cad.opening: Interrupted at plank edges and bevels
cad.load: Wear surface distributing contact into plank core

notes: Wear class is evidence attached to the selected product, not geometry added to the overlay.

objects.name: laminate decorative print layer
objects.definition: The printed paper or film beneath a laminate wear overlay that supplies the visible timber, stone or abstract pattern.
functions: Provide the plank's visible design
Align repeated or varied pattern imagery
Remain protected beneath the transparent overlay

cad.pattern: Thin printed field on each plank with a selected repeat or randomisation
cad.placement: Between wear overlay and HDF core
cad.opening: Stops at plank edges
cad.load: Decorative layer with negligible structural role

notes: The printed image should not cause a material take-off system to classify laminate as the depicted timber or stone.

objects.name: laminate high-density fibreboard core
objects.definition: The dense wood-fibre board body of a laminate plank, machined to form its locking edges and carrying most of the plank thickness and stiffness.
functions: Support the wear and decorative layers
Carry the click-lock profile
Distribute local bending and joint loads

cad.pattern: Main plank body with profiled edges
cad.placement: Between decor layer and balancing underside
cad.opening: Machined at click edges
cad.load: Primary plank body carrying local structural action within the floating surface

notes: The core is wood-based but its water resistance and emissions are selected-product evidence.

objects.name: laminate balancing layer
objects.definition: The resin-impregnated underside layer of a laminate plank that balances stresses and protects the lower face of the fibreboard core.
functions: Balance the layered plank construction
Reduce distortion from unequal face stresses
Provide a consistent underside against underlay

cad.pattern: Continuous thin underside layer on each plank
cad.placement: Below HDF core and above separate underlay
cad.opening: Interrupted at profiled edges
cad.load: Balancing and protective layer, not separate cushioning

notes: Backing is ambiguous; this object is the factory balancing layer, not site-laid underlay.

objects.name: hybrid rigid-core floor plank
objects.definition: A factory-made click-together plank with a rigid polymer-composite core, decorative surface, transparent wear layer and optional factory-attached underlay.
functions: Form one repeated unit of a hybrid floating floor
Carry a rigid click joint
Provide a timber-look or stone-look resilient surface over a rigid core

cad.pattern: Repeated click-locked planks in a floating raft
cad.placement: Over prepared substrate with attached or separate underlay
cad.opening: Cut around fixed elements while preserving raft movement
cad.load: Rigid composite finish plank transferring loads through underlay

notes: Hybrid must store its actual core family because SPC and WPC are physically different.

objects.name: hybrid plank transparent wear layer
objects.definition: The transparent polymer upper layer of a hybrid plank that protects the decorative film and provides the exposed wear surface.
functions: Protect the printed decorative film
Provide the exposed walking face
Carry selected texture and factory surface treatment

cad.pattern: Continuous thin top layer on each rigid plank
cad.placement: Above decorative film
cad.opening: Interrupted at plank edges and bevels
cad.load: Wear surface transferring contact into core

notes: Nominal wear-layer thickness and tested performance remain product evidence.

objects.name: hybrid plank decorative film
objects.definition: A printed polymer film beneath the transparent wear layer of a hybrid plank that supplies its timber, stone or abstract visual pattern.
functions: Provide the visible printed design
Coordinate board-to-board pattern variation
Remain protected beneath the wear layer

cad.pattern: Thin printed field across each plank
cad.placement: Between rigid core and transparent wear layer
cad.opening: Stops at plank edges
cad.load: Decorative layer with negligible structural role

notes: The image must not drive material classification as timber or stone.

objects.name: stone-polymer composite flooring core
objects.definition: A dense rigid hybrid-plank core made from polymer mixed with mineral filler and machined to form the plank body and locking edges.
functions: Provide rigidity and dimensional body
Carry the click-lock profile
Support decorative and wear layers
materials: calcium carbonate or other mineral filler

cad.pattern: Main dense body of each SPC plank with machined edges
cad.placement: Below decorative film and above attached underlay if present
cad.opening: Machined at click edges
cad.load: Primary rigid plank body carrying local board and joint loads

notes: Stone in the market name refers to mineral filler and must not be counted as a natural stone floor finish.

objects.name: wood-polymer composite flooring core
objects.definition: A rigid or semi-rigid hybrid-plank core made from polymer and wood-derived filler, forming the board body and locking profile.
functions: Provide plank thickness and stiffness
Carry the click-lock edge
Support the decorative and wear layers

cad.pattern: Main composite body of each WPC plank with machined edges
cad.placement: Below decorative film and above attached underlay if present
cad.opening: Machined at click edges
cad.load: Primary plank body carrying local board and joint loads

notes: WPC core flooring and external wood-plastic decking have different product roles and exposure requirements.

objects.name: factory-attached plank underlay
objects.definition: A thin foam, cork or resilient backing factory bonded to the underside of an individual floating-floor plank rather than laid as a separate continuous roll.
functions: Provide local cushioning beneath each plank
Reduce the need for a separate underlay only where the selected system allows
Remain aligned with the plank module and its joints

cad.pattern: One backing pad aligned to each plank underside
cad.placement: Factory bonded below the plank core
cad.opening: Stops short of click edges as selected
cad.load: Local resilient support transferring load to the subfloor

notes: Attached underlay creates repeated plank-sized pads, not necessarily one continuous acoustic layer across joints.

objects.name: strand-woven bamboo floorboard
objects.definition: A dense factory-made flooring board formed by compressing and bonding bamboo strands, commonly machined for floating or direct-fixed installation.
functions: Provide a bamboo-based hard floor surface
Join as a plank system
Remain distinct from solid timber and printed timber-look products

cad.pattern: Repeated parallel or patterned planks
cad.placement: Joined as floating floor or direct fixed according to the selected product
cad.opening: Cut around fixed construction while preserving movement zones
cad.load: Finish plank transferring load to underlay or adhesive

notes: Bamboo is a grass-based engineered flooring material and should not be costed or described automatically as solid timber.

objects.name: carpet soft underlay
objects.definition: A resilient fibrous, foam, rubber or combination layer installed between a prepared subfloor and stretch-in textile floor covering.
functions: Cushion the carpet
Absorb repeated footfall energy
Separate the carpet backing from the hard subfloor

cad.pattern: Continuous butted roll field within the gripper perimeter
cad.placement: Above prepared subfloor and below stretch-in carpet
cad.opening: Trim around fixed elements and stop at gripper strips
cad.load: Compressible support beneath the tensioned carpet

notes: The underlay classification and compatibility belong to the selected carpet-underlay pair.

objects.name: fibrous carpet underlay
objects.definition: A soft carpet underlay made primarily from bonded textile, wool, synthetic or recycled fibre rather than cellular foam or crumb rubber.
functions: Cushion textile floor covering
Absorb impact through a fibrous structure
Provide thermal and acoustic contribution as selected

cad.pattern: Butted fibrous rolls or sheets under the carpet field
cad.placement: Within stretch-in carpet gripper perimeter
cad.opening: Trim around fixed objects
cad.load: Compressible fibrous support layer

notes: Felt is accepted as a related family term because not every fibrous underlay is made by the same process.

objects.name: foam carpet underlay
objects.definition: A cellular polymer underlay installed beneath stretch-in carpet to provide cushioning and repeated compression recovery.
functions: Cushion the carpet under footfall
Protect carpet backing from the hard substrate
Provide selected thickness and recovery

cad.pattern: Continuous butted foam roll field below carpet
cad.placement: Within stretch-in carpet gripper perimeter
cad.opening: Trim around fixed elements
cad.load: Compressible cellular support layer

notes: Carpet and hard-floor foam underlays may look alike in section but have different compression and system roles.

objects.name: rubber-crumb carpet underlay
objects.definition: A resilient carpet underlay formed from bonded rubber crumb or a rubber-rich composite and supplied in rolls or sheets.
functions: Cushion the carpet
Recover under repeated loading
Provide a dense resilient layer beneath textile flooring

cad.pattern: Continuous butted rubber-composite roll field
cad.placement: Below stretch-in carpet within the gripper perimeter
cad.opening: Trim around fixed construction
cad.load: Dense resilient cushioning layer

notes: Rubber material alone does not make this an exposed rubber floor finish.

objects.name: broadloom carpet
objects.definition: A textile floor covering manufactured in broad rolls and cut into room-sized pieces for stretch-in or bonded installation with planned seams.
functions: Provide the exposed textile walking surface
Cover large room areas with relatively few seams
Carry pile direction, pattern repeat and backing as one product

cad.pattern: Broad room-sized sheets with directional pile and planned seams
cad.placement: Over soft underlay or bonded directly to prepared subfloor
cad.opening: Cut around walls, stairs and penetrations
cad.load: Textile wear layer transferring traffic to underlay or adhesive

notes: Broadloom describes manufacturing width and installation format, not fibre or pile style.

objects.name: carpet pile layer
objects.definition: The exposed field of yarn loops, cut tufts or woven yarn rising above the carpet backing and forming the walked-on textile surface.
functions: Provide the visible and tactile carpet surface
Receive foot traffic
Create cut, loop or combined surface texture

cad.pattern: Dense repeated yarn field across the carpet backing
cad.placement: Above the carpet backing
cad.opening: Interrupted at seams, cuts and module edges
cad.load: Wear layer transmitting footfall into backing

notes: Low-detail SketchUp display may use a surface material while retaining actual pile height and direction in data.

objects.name: carpet primary backing
objects.definition: The base fabric through which carpet yarn is tufted or otherwise anchored before any secondary backing is applied.
functions: Hold tufted yarn positions
Establish carpet gauge and pattern
Provide the first structural textile layer beneath the pile

cad.pattern: Continuous textile sheet immediately below the pile
cad.placement: Within the carpet product above secondary backing
cad.opening: Cut at carpet edges and seams
cad.load: Anchors yarn and distributes pile loads

notes: Primary and secondary backings may be hidden in ordinary drawing detail but matter for seam and adhesive compatibility.

objects.name: carpet secondary backing
objects.definition: The stabilising backing layer bonded beneath the primary carpet backing to add dimensional stability, strength and an installation-compatible underside.
functions: Stabilise the carpet construction
Protect tuft anchorage
Provide the underside that contacts underlay or adhesive

cad.pattern: Continuous underside layer of the broadloom product
cad.placement: Below the primary backing
cad.opening: Cut at carpet edges and seams
cad.load: Stabilises and transfers textile loads to the installed support

notes: Secondary backing is factory part of the carpet, not the separate underlay installed on site.

objects.name: tufted carpet
objects.definition: A carpet construction in which yarn is inserted through a primary backing and secured before a stabilising underside or secondary backing is applied.
functions: Provide a machine-tufted textile walking surface
Form cut, loop or combined pile styles
Carry pile and backing as one manufactured product

cad.pattern: Continuous or modular tufted textile field
cad.placement: As broadloom, tile or plank finish
cad.opening: Cut at room or module boundaries
cad.load: Textile finish transferring traffic through its backing

notes: Some tufted constructions are modular; the product format remains a separate attribute from manufacturing method.

objects.name: woven carpet
objects.definition: A carpet in which face yarns and structural backing yarns are interlaced during weaving to create an integrated textile floor covering.
functions: Provide an integrated woven textile surface
Carry pattern and backing structure through the weave
Install as broadloom or another selected woven format

cad.pattern: Broad woven textile sheets with pattern direction
cad.placement: Over underlay or bonded as selected
cad.opening: Cut around fixed construction
cad.load: Integrated woven finish transferring traffic to installed support

notes: Woven describes manufacturing construction, not whether the carpet is wool or synthetic.

objects.name: cut-pile carpet surface
objects.definition: A carpet face in which the yarn loops are cut so individual yarn ends form the exposed pile surface.
functions: Provide a soft cut-yarn walking surface
Create twist, plush or other cut-pile texture
Expose pile direction for seam and layout coordination

cad.pattern: Dense field of cut yarn ends
cad.placement: Above carpet backing
cad.opening: Interrupted at product edges and seams
cad.load: Exposed textile wear surface

notes: Cut pile is a surface construction, not a fibre specification.

objects.name: loop-pile carpet surface
objects.definition: A carpet face in which yarn remains as closed loops anchored into or woven with the backing rather than being cut into exposed ends.
functions: Provide a looped textile walking surface
Create level or multi-level loop texture
Expose loop direction and pattern for layout coordination

cad.pattern: Dense repeated yarn loops across the backing
cad.placement: Above carpet backing
cad.opening: Interrupted at product edges and seams
cad.load: Exposed textile wear surface

notes: Loop pile remains a surface style and does not specify whether the carpet is tufted or woven.

objects.name: carpet tile
objects.definition: A factory-made square or rectangular modular textile floor covering with a dimensionally stable backing, installed unit by unit on a floor grid.
functions: Form one replaceable module of a carpet-tile floor
Carry pile direction and backing within a discrete unit
Allow monolithic, quarter-turn or other layout patterns
materials: bitumen-free composite or other stable backing

cad.pattern: Repeated square or rectangular modules on a set-out grid
cad.placement: Retained to a prepared subfloor
cad.opening: Cut modules around fixed penetrations
cad.load: Modular textile finish transferring load through backing and adhesive

notes: Direction is stored per tile because the same product can form different visual layouts.

objects.name: carpet plank
objects.definition: A long rectangular modular textile floor covering with a stable backing, installed in repeated straight, ashlar, herringbone or other plank layouts.
functions: Form one elongated textile module
Support directional modular patterns
Allow local replacement where the installed system permits

cad.pattern: Repeated elongated modules in selected bond or parquet layout
cad.placement: Retained to a prepared subfloor
cad.opening: Cut around fixed elements
cad.load: Modular textile finish transferring load through its backing

notes: Carpet plank is classified by modular format, not by imitation of timber-board material.

objects.name: carpet tile cushion backing
objects.definition: A resilient factory-applied backing beneath a carpet tile or plank that adds cushioning and thickness within the individual module.
functions: Cushion each modular unit
Provide an installation-compatible underside
Contribute to selected acoustic and comfort performance

cad.pattern: One resilient backing pad aligned to each carpet module
cad.placement: Factory bonded below carpet tile or plank
cad.opening: Stops at module edges
cad.load: Local resilient support within each module

notes: Module backing is not a continuous room-wide underlay and joints can affect assembly behaviour.

objects.name: carpet gripper strip
objects.definition: A narrow timber or composite strip carrying angled pins and fixed around room edges to retain the stretched backing of broadloom carpet.
functions: Anchor the stretched carpet perimeter
Maintain a tuck gap at adjacent skirting or trim
Transfer carpet tension into the subfloor

cad.pattern: Continuous or segmented runs around stretch-in carpet perimeter
cad.placement: Fixed to subfloor near walls, frames and transitions
cad.opening: Stops or changes at doorways and stairs
cad.load: Transfers carpet tension into the subfloor through its fixings

notes: Smooth edge is accepted Australian trade language but does not mean the pin-bearing face is smooth.

objects.name: carpet gripper pin
objects.definition: A short angled steel pin projecting from a carpet gripper strip to engage and retain the backing of stretched carpet.
functions: Penetrate or catch the carpet backing
Resist carpet pull away from the perimeter
Transfer tension into the gripper base

cad.pattern: Repeated angled pins along each gripper strip
cad.placement: Factory set into gripper base and angled toward the wall
cad.opening: Absent at strip cuts and excluded zones
cad.load: Transfers carpet tension into the gripper member

notes: Gripper pins and the fasteners that attach the strip to the subfloor are separate objects.

objects.name: broadloom carpet seam
objects.definition: The joined meeting line between adjacent broadloom carpet pieces, aligned to pile and pattern and reinforced or bonded by the selected seam system.
functions: Join separate carpet widths
Maintain pile direction and pattern continuity
Protect cut edges from separation or fraying

cad.pattern: Linear planned joins between broadloom pieces
cad.placement: Within room carpet field and away from unsuitable stress locations as designed
cad.opening: Stops at carpet perimeter or another seam
cad.load: Transfers in-plane carpet tension across the joined cut edges

notes: Seam visibility is an appearance outcome; the physical tape, adhesive and sealed cut edges remain modelled.

objects.name: carpet seam tape
objects.definition: A reinforced strip placed beneath adjoining broadloom carpet edges to support and bond a heat-seamed or otherwise documented carpet joint.
functions: Bridge the carpet seam underside
Carry hot-melt or other seam adhesive
Reinforce the joined cut edges

cad.pattern: Continuous strip centred beneath each broadloom seam
cad.placement: Between underlay and carpet backing
cad.opening: Stops at perimeter or seam intersection
cad.load: Reinforces and bonds the seam underside

notes: Seam tape is not a visible transition strip.

objects.name: carpet seam hot-melt adhesive
objects.definition: A thermoplastic adhesive carried on seam tape and melted during installation to bond the underside of adjoining broadloom carpet edges.
functions: Bond carpet backing to seam tape
Set into a continuous seam connection
Transfer carpet tension through the reinforced joint

cad.pattern: Continuous melted adhesive field on seam tape beneath the joined edges
